correctness.rationale: For all full-dimensional finite coaxial ball intersections, the squared section radius is -z² plus a concave lower envelope of affine functions, so active center C(z) decreases. Integration by parts with boundary-zero section power proves v_perp−v_parallel=−Cov(Z,C(Z)); the independent-copy sign identity and positive marginal density establish sign and equality iff a ball. Expanding C into downward jumps gives exactly the positive conditional-mean sum. Every endpoint, normalized variance, dimensional factor and redundant-ball case was checked. Symbolic three-ball integrals and 138 independent finite checker assertions pass; finite tests supplement the universal analytic proof.

value.rationale: The geometric question asks whether the centroidal covariance ellipsoid of any finite intersection of collinear-centered balls, even with unequal radii and no reflection symmetry, is flattened along its center line. A sharp all-dimensional inequality with ball equality rigidity and a strictly positive contribution from every effective center switch gives an interpretable structural mechanism, not a mere computed example. The exact three-active-ball case is genuinely outside the previously known symmetric two-ball theorem. No theorem for general noncollinear intersections is implied.
